question: Which organization presents the Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award?
answer: The Baseball Writers' Association of America (BBWAA).
source_title: Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award
evidence: The award has been presented by the Baseball Writers' Association of America (BBWAA) since 1931.

question: Why was Kenesaw Mountain Landis's name removed from the MVP plaque?
answer: Because several former MVP winners complained to the BBWAA about Landis's role against the integration of MLB.
source_title: Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award
evidence: Starting in 2020, Landis' name no longer appears on the MVP plaque, after the BBWAA received complaints from several former MVP winners about Landis' role against the integration of MLB.

question: Why was the Chalmers Award discontinued?
answer: Because it was not as effective at advertising as Hugh Chalmers had hoped.
source_title: Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award
evidence: Since the award was not as effective at advertising as Chalmers had hoped, it was discontinued after 1914.

question: What effect did the voting criteria of the American League's 1920s League Award have on Babe Ruth?
answer: Because voters had to pick one player per team and prior winners were ineligible, Ruth won only a single award.
source_title: Major League Baseball Most Valuable Player Award
evidence: Voters were required to select one player from each team, and player-coaches and prior award winners were ineligible. Famously, these criteria resulted in Babe Ruth winning only a single MVP award before it was dropped after 1928.

question: Who won the first national Rookie of the Year Award, and what was the award later renamed?
answer: Jackie Robinson of the Brooklyn Dodgers; the award was renamed the Jackie Robinson Award.
source_title: Major League Baseball Rookie of the Year Award
evidence: The award became national in 1947; Jackie Robinson, the Brooklyn Dodgers' second baseman, won the inaugural award. The award was renamed the Jackie Robinson Award in July 1987, 40 years after Robinson broke the baseball color line.

question: Why has the Rookie of the Year Award been criticized for going to players with Nippon Professional Baseball experience?
answer: Some feel past NPB players are not true rookies because of their previous professional experience, since rookie status counts only Major League experience.
source_title: Major League Baseball Rookie of the Year Award
evidence: The current definition of rookie status for the award is based only on Major League experience, but some feel that past NPB players are not true rookies because of their past professional experience.

question: How do supporters of awarding former NPB players the Rookie of the Year Award counter the criticism?
answer: They point out that the award's first recipient and namesake, Jackie Robinson, played in the Negro leagues before MLB and so could not be considered a "true rookie" either.
source_title: Major League Baseball Rookie of the Year Award
evidence: Others, however, believe it should make no difference since the first recipient and the award's namesake played for the Negro leagues before his MLB career and thus could also not be considered a "true rookie".

question: Which two teams played in the first modern World Series?
answer: The AL champion Boston Americans (now the Boston Red Sox) and the NL champion Pittsburgh Pirates.
evidence: The 1903 World Series was the first modern World Series to be played in Major League Baseball. It matched the American League (AL) champion Boston Americans (now the Boston Red Sox) against the National League (NL) champion Pittsburgh Pirates in a best-of-nine series, with Boston prevailing five games to three, winning the last four.

question: Why did the losing Pittsburgh players receive a larger individual share of the 1903 World Series gate receipts than the winners?
answer: Because Pirates owner Barney Dreyfuss added his own share of the gate receipts to the players' share.
evidence: Pirates owner Barney Dreyfuss added his share of the gate receipts to the players' share, so the losing team's players actually finished with a larger individual share than the winning team's.

question: What effect did the 1903 World Series have on the standing of the American League?
answer: It brought the new league prestige, proving its best could beat the National League's best and strengthening demand for future World Series.
evidence: The Series brought the new American League prestige and proved its best could beat the best of the National League, thus strengthening the demand for future World Series competitions.

question: Why did the 2001 World Series begin later than usual?
answer: Because the regular season was delayed after the September 11 attacks.
evidence: The Series began later than usual, as a result of a delay in the regular season after the September 11 attacks, and it was the first to extend into November.

question: Which Diamondbacks pitchers were named Most Valuable Players of the 2001 World Series?
evidence: Diamondbacks pitchers Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling were both named World Series Most Valuable Players.
